prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean (A) a beginner-friendly explainer site that uses real numbers in examples, or (B) an educator that publishes its own trading/account performance (including losses), or (C) a site that documents real-world losses/hacks and post‑mortems so you can learn from them?

Quick suggestions that cover those needs:

- If you want plain‑English, beginner guides that use real numbers: Coin Bureau (clear, long-form guides and videos) and Bankless (good for DeFi basics). They explain concepts in everyday language and walk through numeric examples.

- If you want data-driven on‑chain numbers and charts (not P&L of a teacher, but transparent metrics): Glassnode Academy and IntoTheBlock. Great for seeing real metrics and charts explained in plain terms.

- If you want educators who publish trade ideas and keep public trade logs (wins and losses): CryptoCred (Twitter/YouTube) and some TradingView educators — look for people who keep a public trading journal or pinned records.

- If you want to learn from real failures/hacks and see the actual loss figures and post‑mortems: Rekt (rekt.news) and individual post‑mortems on hacks (Poly Network, Wormhole, etc.). These are blunt and numeric — very useful for risk lessons.

If you tell me which of A/B/C you mean, I’ll give a single “best” recommendation and one or two concrete links that match exactly what you want.
